toc.title: Audit Logs: What an Auditor Needs
Integrating Services for Logging at Scale (skill 4.4.5)

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. EMR: Elastic MapReduce; VPC: Virtual Private Cloud; ECS: Elastic Container Service; MWAA: Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow; KMS: Key Management Service; IAM: Identity and Access Management; ELB: Elastic Load Balancing; URI: Uniform Resource Identifier; SNS: Simple Notification Service

  • Use AWS CloudTrail to track API calls
  • Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs to store application logs
  • Use AWS CloudTrail Lake for centralized logging queries
  • Analyze logs with Athena, CloudWatch Logs Insights and Amazon OpenSearch Service
  • Integrate AWS services for logging, including Amazon EMR for large volumes of logs

2Audit Logs: What an Auditor Needs

Running case

Kestrel Freight Faces an Audit

  • An auditor asks: who read the customer table last March, and who changed the bucket policy?
  • Logs are scattered: some in S3, some in CloudWatch, some in application files
  • Retention is inconsistent, and one team deleted logs to save cost
  • Your job: make the logs complete, protected, searchable and retained
Audit question Evidence AWS source
Who called which API, when, from where? API activity AWS CloudTrail
Who read or wrote which object or item? Data-plane activity CloudTrail data events, S3 server access logs, database audit logs
What did the application or job do? Application and job logs CloudWatch Logs
What changed in the configuration? Configuration history AWS Config (Module 18)
What network traffic occurred? Flow records VPC Flow Logs

A good audit log is complete (the right events are on), accurate (not altered), retained (for the required period), protected (restricted access), and searchable (queryable on demand).

Exam tip

Auditors ask who, what, when: CloudTrail answers it for API calls; data events are needed for object-level access and are off by default.

3AWS CloudTrail: Tracking API Calls (skill 4.4.1)

  • Event types: management events (control plane such as creating or deleting resources and changing policies; recorded by default), data events (S3 object-level, Lambda invocations, DynamoDB item-level and more; off by default, extra cost), Insights events (unusual API activity), and network activity events
  • Event history: the console shows the last 90 days of management events per Region for free [Verify live]; it is not enough for audits
  • Trails: a trail delivers events continuously to an S3 bucket (and optionally CloudWatch Logs and EventBridge): create a multi-Region trail, and an organization trail to cover every account in AWS Organizations
  • Protect the logs: deliver to a dedicated, encrypted S3 bucket (ideally in a separate log-archive account), restrict and deny deletes, use S3 Object Lock or versioning, and turn on log file validation (digest files with hashes and signatures show no log file was changed or removed)
  • Delivery time: events typically arrive in about five minutes (not guaranteed)
  • Data events for audits: enable them on the sensitive buckets, tables and functions (selectors let you scope them to avoid cost)
Exam tip

"Prove who read objects in a sensitive bucket" → CloudTrail data events on that bucket, delivered to a protected S3 bucket with log file validation.

4CloudWatch Logs for Application Logs (skill 4.4.2)

  • CloudWatch Logs stores application and job logs from Lambda, Glue, ECS, EMR, MWAA, Step Functions and EC2 (agent); organize log groups by application and environment
  • For audit use:
    • Write structured logs with who, what, when, run ID and record counts (never secrets or raw personal data)
    • Set retention to meet policy (the default is never expire, which is costly but safe; too short loses evidence)
    • Encrypt the log group with KMS and restrict access with IAM
    • Send a copy to S3 for long-term storage: export tasks or subscription filters through Firehose
    • Data protection policies can find and mask sensitive data in logs Beyond the guide
  • CloudWatch Logs and CloudTrail can be combined: send a trail to CloudWatch Logs to alarm on sensitive API calls (Module 12)

5AWS CloudTrail Lake: Centralized Queries (skill 4.4.3)Verify live]** **[Dates

  • AWS CloudTrail Lake lets you run SQL queries directly on events without building your own S3 and Athena setup
  • Event data stores: immutable collections of events, converted to Apache ORC (columnar); each store holds one event category: CloudTrail events (management, data, network activity), Insights events, AWS Config configuration items, AWS Audit Manager evidence, or events from outside AWS (ingested with PutAuditEvents through a channel)
  • Centralize: an organization event data store collects events from all accounts and Regions; queries can join several stores; a resource policy gives cross-account access
  • Retention (set by the pricing option): up to 3,653 days (about 10 years) with one-year extendable retention pricing, or up to 2,557 days (about 7 years) with seven-year retention pricing
  • Queries: SQL (Trino SELECT syntax) with saved queries, sample queries, natural-language query generation, results kept for seven days and savable to S3; dashboards (managed, custom, highlights); you pay per data scanned
  • Compared with Event history: Lake spans accounts and Regions, many attributes, and long retention
  • Federation: federate an event data store so Athena can query it through the Glue Data Catalog
  • Encryption: events are encrypted by default, or with your KMS key (cannot be changed later)
  • Availability [Dates]: CloudTrail Lake stops accepting new customers from 31 May 2026; existing customers continue. For new setups the usual alternative is a trail to S3 queried with Athena (below)
Trail to S3 + Athena CloudTrail Lake
Setup Build it yourself (bucket, table, partitions) Managed event data store and SQL
Cost shape S3 storage + Athena per data scanned Ingestion and storage fees + query per data scanned
Retention As long as you keep the files Up to about 7 or 10 years by option
Multi-account Organization trail to one bucket Organization event data store
Best for Cheap, flexible, long-term archive Fast, centralized, managed audit queries
Exam tip

"Centralized SQL queries over CloudTrail events from many accounts, with no infrastructure to build" → CloudTrail Lake (organization event data store).

6Analyzing Logs (skill 4.4.4)

Tool Use it for Notes
Amazon Athena SQL on logs in S3 (CloudTrail, S3 access logs, ELB, VPC Flow Logs, exported CloudWatch logs) Create the table (CloudTrail has a ready-made table template), partition by date or use partition projection, store logs as Parquet for cost; pay per data scanned
CloudWatch Logs Insights Interactive queries on log groups in CloudWatch fields, filter, stats, sort, limit, parse; best for recent logs
Amazon OpenSearch Service Near-real-time search, correlation and dashboards Ingest with Firehose or CloudWatch subscription filters
Amazon EMR Very large volumes and custom processing of logs Spark parses, enriches and writes Parquet back to S3 
-- Athena: who deleted tables in the last day (CloudTrail table)
SELECT useridentity.arn, eventname, eventtime, sourceipaddress
FROM   cloudtrail_logs
WHERE  eventname = 'DeleteTable' AND eventtime > '2026-11-06T00:00:00Z'
ORDER BY eventtime DESC;

7Integrating Services for Logging at Scale (skill 4.4.5)

  • Collect: CloudTrail trail → S3; CloudWatch Logs subscription filter → Kinesis Data Streams or Data Firehose → S3 or OpenSearch; S3 server access logs, ELB and CloudFront logs, VPC Flow Logs → S3 or CloudWatch Logs; Glue and EMR logs → CloudWatch Logs and S3
  • Centralize in one log bucket or account with encryption, retention and restricted access; use AWS Organizations features (organization trails, centralized logging patterns)
  • Large volumes: EMR (Spark) or Glue parse, filter, enrich and convert to partitioned Parquet, so Athena queries are cheap and fast; Firehose can convert to Parquet and partition on delivery
  • Amazon EMR in particular: EMR can write its own logs to S3 (log URI) and process large log datasets from other services
  • Govern the logs themselves: log access to the logs (who read the audit trail), alarm on changes to trails and log groups, and test restores and queries before an audit
Exam tip

"Terabytes of application logs must be parsed and made queryable cheaply" → an EMR or Glue Spark job that writes partitioned Parquet to S3, queried with Athena.

8Exam Q&A

8.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1An auditor asks who downloaded objects from a sensitive S3 bucket during the last year. Which preparation provides this evidence?

  • ACloudTrail management events only, delivered to CloudWatch Logs
  • BThe 90-day CloudTrail event history in the console
  • CCloudTrail data events for that bucket, delivered by a trail to a protected S3 bucket
  • DS3 Lifecycle rules that keep a record of each transition
Show the answer

Answer: C. Object-level reads are data events, which are off by default and must be enabled; a trail retains them beyond the 90-day event history.

S2A security team needs centralized SQL queries over CloudTrail events from all accounts in an organization, with no infrastructure to build and retention of several years. Which option fits?

  • AAmazon CloudWatch metrics filtered by account and Region
  • BAmazon S3 Inventory reports for the log buckets of each account
  • CAmazon Macie sensitive data discovery jobs on the log buckets
  • DCloudTrail Lake with an organization event data store
Show the answer

Answer: D. CloudTrail Lake stores events in managed event data stores that can span an organization and be queried with SQL; note that Lake is closed to new customers from 31 May 2026, so a trail to S3 queried with Athena is the alternative for new setups.

S3An organization generates terabytes of application logs per day that must be parsed and enriched before analysis. Which approach is most appropriate?

  • AOpen each log file in a text editor and search for the errors
  • BStore the logs in the environment variables of a Lambda function
  • CSend every log line to an Amazon SNS topic and read the emails
  • DParse the logs with an EMR or Glue Spark job, write partitioned Parquet to S3, and query with Athena
Show the answer

Answer: D. Spark on EMR or Glue handles very large volumes and produces partitioned columnar data that Athena can query cheaply.

9Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
CloudTrail Management events (on by default), data events (off by default; S3 objects, Lambda, DynamoDB), Insights; event history 90 days; trail → S3 (+ CloudWatch Logs); multi-Region and organization trails; log file validation
Protect logs Separate log-archive account, encrypted bucket, restricted/deny delete, Object Lock, versioning
CloudWatch Logs Log groups, retention (default never expire), KMS, export / subscription → S3, Logs Insights, data protection policies
CloudTrail Lake Event data stores (ORC, immutable), SQL (Trino), organization store, retention up to 7 or 10 years by pricing option, dashboards, federate to Athena; closed to new customers from 31 May 2026
Analysis Athena (SQL on S3, partition/Parquet), Logs Insights, OpenSearch (search, dashboards), EMR/Glue Spark (huge volumes → Parquet)
Integration Subscription filters / Firehose → S3 or OpenSearch, trail → S3, central log bucket/account, Firehose converts to Parquet
